newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan has no plans to import more sugar in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan has no plans to import more sugar in 1996.

text.p: The state-run Trading Corporation of Pakistan said on Tuesday it did not plan to import more sugar in calendar 1996 after having finalised deals to buy 225,000 tonnes for shipment by the end of October.
"We are not considering importing more sugar in 1996 as the country's own sugar mills will start production early next month," an official with the corporation said.

The corporation imported 225,000 tonnes of sugar and the private sector 150,000 tonnes to meet a shortfall, owing to lower production, estimated at 2.47 million tonnes in 1995/96 (July-June), compared to 3.0 million in 1994/95.

One private importer said there was no need to import more sugar in calendar 1996. But he added at least 250,000 tonnes was likely to be imported in 1997 to meet an estimated shortage of 250,000 tonnes after the sugarcane crushing season ends in May next year.
"I think there will be a shortage of 250,000 tonnes in (calendar) 1997 and Pakistan has to import it," said Mohammad Ebrahim Hasham of Mehran Sugar Mills.

He said the shortage was likely to occur as farmers had set up sugarcane crushers at farms to produce brown "Gur" (molasses) instead of selling sugarcane to sugar mills because of high demand for Gur in Afghanistan and Central Asia.

The Pakistan Sugar Mills Association has said stocks of refined crystal white sugar from the 1995/96 production of 2.47 million tonnes fell to 0.1 million by September 30. Mills plan to produce 2.7 million tonnes in 1996/97.

Dealers had lifted 2.36 million tonnes, or 95.81 percent, of the produced sugar and the remaining 4.19 percent, remained within the mills, the Islamabad-based association said. Sugar mills plan to start crushing sugarcane early next month.
At least five ships carrying 59,505 tonnes of sugar were waiting off the Karachi Port for unloading, port officials said.
